input.evidence:
app/main.py:15-16: the route `/orders/search` is registered with no auth decorator or check, and the docstring at line 17 says it backs the storefront's *public* order lookup page. app/main.py:18: `customer = request.args.get("customer", "")` is taken straight from the HTTP query string. Nothing validates or escapes it. app/main.py:20: it is put into the SQL with an f-string inside single quotes: `... WHERE customer_email = '{customer}'`. app/main.py:21: the query runs via `conn.execute(query)`, which is a sqlite3 connection from app/db.py:8-11. app/main.py:22: every returned row goes back to the caller as JSON.
Exploit: `GET /orders/search?customer=' OR '1'='1` returns every order for every customer. A UNION payload such as `' UNION SELECT name, sql, type FROM sqlite_master--` (three columns, matching id/total/status) can read the schema and other tables. sqlite3's `execute()` refuses multiple statements, so stacked queries like `; DROP TABLE` are not possible. The impact is reading data (customer order data and any other table in the DB), with no login needed.
input.recommended_fix: Use a parameterized query: `conn.execute("SELECT id, total, status FROM orders WHERE customer_email = ?", (customer,))`. Add a regression test that sends `' OR '1'='1` and asserts that nothing comes back. Separate design issue: even after the fix, this public endpoint returns any customer's orders to anyone who knows or guesses their email. Consider requiring an order number plus email, or a signed-in session, and add rate limiting.
input.title: SQL injection in public /orders/search via the `customer` query parameter

input.evidence: app/main.py:28: the user-controlled `key = request.args.get("status", "open")` is used only as a dictionary lookup key. app/main.py:29: `status = REPORT_STATUSES.get(key, "OPEN")`. The result is always one of the hardcoded constants defined at app/main.py:8-12 ("OPEN", "SHIPPED", "REFUNDED"), with "OPEN" as the default. app/main.py:31: only that constant is put into the f-string, so attacker input can never reach the SQL text. Nothing else writes to REPORT_STATUSES; it is module-level and only read. Side note: this route has no authentication either (app/main.py:25-26), even though its docstring calls it an operations dashboard. Anyone can see the order counts, but that is not SQL injection.
input.recommended_fix: No security fix needed for CWE-89. Optional hardening so scanners stop flagging it and it stays safe if the allowlist changes later: `conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE status = ?", (status,))`. Separately, decide whether this ops-dashboard endpoint should require authentication.
input.title: False positive: /reports/status interpolates only allowlisted constant values

input.evidence: tests/test_search.py:13: the f-string INSERT puts in `i` (an integer from enumerate) and `email` from `SEED_EMAILS`. That is a hardcoded constant list at tests/test_search.py:7 (["ana@example.com", "li@example.com"]). tests/test_search.py:10-14: `seed()` is called only from the test at line 20, against a temporary DB in pytest's tmp_path (lines 18-19). This is test-only code, not shipped or reachable over HTTP, and no external input reaches it.
input.recommended_fix: No security fix needed. Optionally switch to `conn.execute("INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?, 10.0, 'OPEN')", (i, email))` to model good practice and quiet the scanner, or exclude tests/ from this rule. Also worth adding a test for the F-001 injection payload in this file.
input.title: False positive: f-string SQL in test seed helper uses hardcoded fixture data

I triaged all three scanner findings and saved a draft ticket for each; they're waiting for human review. Only F-001 is a real vulnerability. The other two are false positives.

| ID | Location | Verdict | Severity | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-001 | `app/main.py:20` | **Exploitable** | High | The `customer` query parameter (line 18) goes straight into the SQL with an f-string, and the endpoint is public (no login). For example, `?customer=' OR '1'='1` returns every customer's orders, and a UNION query can read other tables. You can't chain extra statements (sqlite3 runs only one per call), so this is a data leak, not data modification. |
| F-002 | `app/main.py:31` | Not exploitable | None | The user's input is only used to look up a hardcoded allowlist (lines 8–12, 29). Only those fixed constants ever reach the SQL. |
| F-003 | `tests/test_search.py:13` | Not exploitable | None | Test-only code that inserts hardcoded fixture data (line 7) into a temporary database. No outside input reaches it. |

**What to do:**
1. Fix F-001 by passing `customer` as a query parameter (`WHERE customer_email = ?`) instead of building the string. Add a regression test that sends the injection payload.
2. Optionally use the same parameter style in F-002 and F-003, so they stay safe if the code changes and the scanner stops flagging them.
3. Two design issues outside the scan:
   - Even after the fix, `/orders/search` lets anyone see a customer's orders if they know or guess the email. It should require an order number or a login, plus rate limiting.
   - `/reports/status` is described as an operations dashboard, but it has no authentication.
